x-summary: Workspace side panel that keeps the page usable: docked column or modeless panel. Modal side panels belong to sf-modal; the modal Drawer mode is deprecated.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-drawer for a workspace side panel next to a page that stays usable: docked (page content shifts, both sides at once) or modal=false (overlapping, no scrim, no focus trap). For a modal side panel use sf-modal with position="inline-start|inline-end".
do_not: Do not use a modal sf-drawer for new interfaces; use sf-modal with a side position
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not use overlay as a substitute for modal semantics
Do not pass literal design dimensions when a standard size or Framework token exists

Content

x-decisions: alias-conflict: vocabulary §5.1 decides drawer:snap → sf-drawer-snapped, a fact of the component (the alias table's sf-drawer-snap is the bare verb of a request the drawer never waits on); the converter's sf-drawer-snap never shipped and gets no row.

detail-adapter: §8 takes page elements out of detail, so the new names carry {drawerId, …} only; each old drawer:* name keeps its old detail (component, drawer, root added) through a split row and the element's detail adapter (sfAliasAdapters). Larena and bx-simai.main listen to drawer:after-open and drawer:after-close (vocabulary §9.2).
version: 1.6.0 → 1.7.0, a minor while the renamed members hold dated aliases (§4.10); added unsaved, dismissible and the snapped detail field.

existing-aliases: compatibility.deprecations folds into aliases.json as documentation rows: the page triggers data-sf-drawer-open/-close/-toggle stay as aliases of data-sf-action (§16.10) and of data-drawer with aria-controls; the modal-like default without docked keeps its own deprecation in the change journal (no alias kind: it is a recommendation, not a name).
template: templates.default names the Lit template in index.js (template()), the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus the docked column, the bottom sheet and the outside close button; probe.json drives Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape (gate 16).

css-variables: the seven variables docs.md and the sheet already promise (background, colour, overlay, gutter, block start, dock breakpoint, z-index); the portal carries their computed values from the host (§19.1). --sf-drawer-radius and --sf-drawer-width stay internal: the sheet sets them per size.
side-effects: the panel draws at the end of body or of its [data-sf-overlay-container] (portal) and, when modal and not docked, locks the page through the layer stack's one lease (locks-page).
layer: kind panel (§19.1); a modal drawer traps focus, a docked or modeless one does not (updateLayer re-declares it when modal or docked changes).
slots: the drawer places the page's own nodes (the content into its body, slot="edge" beside the panel) and never copies them (§4.5); the converter's slot "default" is the content slot.
dismissing: the close request carries {reason, unsaved} (§19.3); dismissible=false removes escape and outside like close-on-esc and close-on-overlay, never an explicit action.
instance ids (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41): a drawer without id or drawer-id takes its path id (sf-drawer-<n> in document order) instead of a random one.
